title: Design, synthesis, and evaluation of natural product-inspired small molecules targeting the serotonin-2C receptor
abstract: Understimulation of the serotonin-2c receptor in the central nervous system has been strongly linked to neurological disorders ranging from opioid addiction to schizophrenia in mice models. Designing a small molecule agonist which upregulates the 2c pathway could prove to be a useful clinical angle in tackling maladaptive behaviors faced by growing segments of the populace. However, the serotonin-2a receptor, a receptor with a similarly-configured binding site for serotonin is known to cause cardiovascular abnormalities when overstimulated by synthetic agonists, molecules that mimic the structure and function of serotonin. Agonists therefore need to be potent and selective for 2c. Starting from yohimbine alkaloids, a class of compounds isolated from the Rauvolfia vomitoria plant, molecules were designed using computational models and synthesized in-house using Pictet-Spengler condensations. These compounds were high-throughput screened using in vitro Ca2+-flux assays and tested on mice models. Preliminary data on ortho-substituted analogs have indicated good binding efficacy and selectivity. One such compound reported has <10nM EC50 and a 6.5 selectivity 2c/2a in vitro, measurables approaching Lorcaserin, the only FDA-approved drug for the 2c receptor to date. Further modifications and improvements to ortho-functionalized analogs are expected to be the next step in optimizing the functional selectivity of serotonin analogs as a potential market pharmaceutical.
